Visit note | 2025-08-24 03:00 PM | Dr. Tanvir Ahmed, General Medicine | Patient: Hossain Chowdhury, 39, male. Mr. Chowdhury returns for review, explaining that he gets breathless when climbing stairs, looks pale, and feels constantly tired. He works as a graphic designer and notes these issues worsened after a long spell of poor meals while living alone in Noakhali. He has a known history of Essential hypertension. On examination, his haemoglobin is 9.8 g/dL, alongside BP 137/96 mmHg, pulse 70 bpm, and weight 93 kg. Cardiovascular and respiratory examinations are otherwise unremarkable. Assessment: Iron deficiency anaemia. Plan: a prescription was issued for iron supplementation. He was advised to eat more lentils, spinach, liver, and eggs, and to avoid tea within an hour of meals. Follow-up in 6 weeks with a repeat haemoglobin.

Visit note | 2025-08-24 03:00 PM | Dr. Arif Hossain, Pulmonology | Patient: Jui Begum, 66, female. Mrs. Begum presents for review, reporting wheezing on walking, a long history of smoking, and breathlessness that has been worse for several days. She works as a farmer and states her symptoms worsened during the dusty dry season in Kamrangirchar. She has no documented comorbidities. Today, she shows confusion and sleepiness with only mild breathlessness. On examination, SpO2 is 89%, BP is 134/82 mmHg, pulse 90 bpm, and weight is 87 kg. Chest auscultation reveals widespread expiratory wheeze. Assessment: COPD exacerbation. Plan: a prescription was issued for bronchodilators and systemic therapy. She was advised to stop smoking completely, avoid cooking smoke, and take the yearly flu vaccine. Follow-up in 1 week, sooner if breathing worsens.

Visit note | 2025-08-24 03:00 PM | Dr. Asif Mahmud, Dermatology | Patient: Hossain Gazi, 21, male. Mr. Gazi attends for his first visit complaining of pimples and blackheads on his face as well as spots on his back. He works as a security guard and mentions the condition has been worse since working in a hot kitchen in Rangpur. He reports no significant past medical history. Examination reveals about 23 inflamed spots on the face, with BP 114/80 mmHg, pulse 83 bpm, and weight 72 kg. Assessment: Acne vulgaris. Plan: a prescription was issued for topical treatment. He was advised to wash his face twice daily with a gentle cleanser and not to squeeze spots. Follow-up in 2 months.

Visit note | 2025-08-24 03:00 PM | Dr. Shahadat Hossain, ENT | Patient: Sukumar Nath, 19, male. Mr. Nath comes in for his first visit with a blocked nose, thick nasal discharge lasting over ten days, and pressure over his cheeks and forehead. He works as a shopkeeper and notes that the trouble started after a cold during a rainy week in Sirajganj. He has a history of Bronchial asthma. On examination, his temperature is 99.5°F, BP 130/85 mmHg, pulse 93 bpm, and weight 64 kg. Sinus tenderness is present on palpation. Assessment: Acute sinusitis. Plan: a prescription was issued for nasal decongestants and supportive care. He was advised to use steam inhalation twice daily and drink warm fluids. Follow-up in 10 days.

Visit note | 2025-08-24 03:00 PM | Dr. Mehedi Hasan, Ophthalmology | Patient: Rashed Siddique, 29, male. Visit note | 2025-08-24 03:30 PM | Dr. Shahadat Hossain, ENT | Patient: Faruk Faruque, 20, male. Mr. Faruque presents for his initial medical evaluation complaining of a sore throat, painful swallowing, and associated fever. He works as a software developer and recalls that his symptoms began after shouting loudly at a cricket match in Lalbagh. He has no significant past medical history or chronic systemic illnesses. On clinical examination, his temperature is recorded at 101.2°F, blood pressure is 134/86 mmHg, pulse rate is elevated at 110 bpm, and his weight is 54 kg. Examination of the oral cavity reveals marked erythema of the tonsils with yellowish exudates and tender anterior cervical lymphadenopathy. The lungs are clear to auscultation, and the abdomen is soft. Assessment: Acute tonsillitis. Plan: a prescription was issued for antibiotic therapy and symptomatic relief. He was advised to gargle frequently with warm salt water, consume soft foods, and drink plenty of fluids to remain well hydrated. Follow-up is scheduled in 1 week, with instructions to seek immediate care if high fever or breathing difficulties develop.

Visit note | 2025-08-24 04:00 PM | Dr. Sabrina Chowdhury, Cardiology | Patient: Eva Ahmed, 72, female. Mrs. Ahmed returns for follow-up, reporting that she gets tired easily and experiences a fluttering sensation in her chest along with an irregular fast heartbeat. She works as a shopkeeper and mentions these episodes started after a sleepless night travelling to Cumilla. She has no known comorbidities. On examination, her pulse is 134 bpm and irregular, BP is 114/78 mmHg, and weight is 61 kg. Heart sounds confirm an irregular rhythm without added murmurs. Assessment: Atrial fibrillation. Plan: a prescription was issued for rate-control medication. She was advised to limit tea and coffee, avoid alcohol, and report any fainting at once. Follow-up in 2 weeks with an ECG and kidney function tests.
